competitions.name: Synapse Arena
competitions.about: An AI/ML racing challenge in which teams train and optimize a Reinforcement Learning agent to navigate a custom racing environment, then compete against other teams in 1v1 races. Points are awarded based on race outcomes and performance.
rules: Teams train their own Reinforcement Learning agent for the custom racing environment.
AI agents compete in 1v1 races.
Points are awarded based on race outcomes and performance; the team with the highest cumulative points wins.

competitions.name: Syntax Sprint
competitions.about: A competitive programming contest organized by PYC Club under the Technical Board of IIIT Bhagalpur. Participants test their algorithmic thinking, problem-solving abilities, and coding efficiency in a coding contest on Codeforces. There is no preliminary online round or shortlisting process.
rules: Participation is individual.
Participants register directly for the offline contest at IIIT Bhagalpur.
The top four performers compete in knockout matches to determine the final rankings.

timeline.desc: Offline coding contest and knockout matches

competitions.name: Bull Run
competitions.about: Bull Run is a trading competition where participants test their market awareness, decision-making, and ability to make strategic trading choices. The goal is to trade smart, manage risk, and aim for the strongest performance.

competitions.name: Aerorush
competitions.about: A drone competition at ProtoFos 2026 where participants bring their flying skills and technical knowledge to the arena. The event focuses on piloting, control, and handling a drone in a competitive setting.

competitions.name: Bot Battleground
competitions.rounds: 3 (Robo Race, Robo Soccer, Tug of War)
competitions.about: A multi-round robotics competition at ProtoFos 2026 where teams design and control a robot across Robo Race, Robo Soccer, and Tug of War. The event tests maneuverability, speed, control, strength, traction, and engineering skill.
rules: Teams must have 3–5 members and use one robot across all three rounds.
Maximum robot dimensions: 500 × 200 × 150 mm (L × W × H).
Maximum robot weight: 5 kg, including batteries and attachments.
The onboard electrical supply must not exceed 12V.
Wireless control is mandatory; mechanical engines are prohibited.
Only minor modifications for Robo Soccer attachments or mechanisms are permitted before the final round.
Participants register directly for the offline competition; there is no preliminary online round or shortlisting process.

timeline.desc: Robo Race, Robo Soccer and Tug of War

competitions.name: Securathon
competitions.about: A cybersecurity hackathon conducted by DevC and Hackelite. Participants identify and solve real-world cybersecurity problems by designing and implementing practical software solutions. Teams are encouraged to use suitable cryptographic algorithms and follow OWASP Top 10 security practices, with an emphasis on security by design.
rules: Build a practical software solution addressing a real-world cybersecurity problem.
Use appropriate cryptographic algorithms where relevant.
Follow OWASP Top 10 security practices.
Projects are evaluated on cryptographic use, security implementation, OWASP Top 10 compliance, technical implementation and design, real-world relevance, and overall quality.

timeline.desc: 24-hour hackathon; 2–4 hours of buffer time may be used if required

competitions.name: Robo Relay
competitions.tagline: One robot. Two mazes. Zero remote.
competitions.fee: Event pass ₹99 (Robo Relay only) or All-Events pass ₹249; food and accommodation not included. Registration via Unstop + payment form (links TBA, keep the register button as a placeholder link).
competitions.eligibility: Open to all engineering students (Teams of 3-5)
competitions.about: An autonomous robotics challenge where precision, speed and intelligent navigation decide the winner. Each team builds ONE autonomous robot that must complete two stages back to back. Stage 1 is a Line Following Robot (LFR) run over a marked path with curves, turns and junctions. Stage 2 is a Maze Solver with thermocol walls, corridors, sharp turns and dead ends, testing navigation, path-planning and decision-making. Robots must run fully autonomously, with no remote control or human guidance once the run begins.
highlights: Autonomous navigation through two different maze environments
Robot design, development and sensor-based control
Line following, obstacle awareness and path planning
Evaluation by total completion time and penalties
A showcase of practical robotics and embedded programming
rules: One timed run through both mazes. Objective: finish both in the shortest time with minimum penalties.
Penalties for navigation errors, wall collisions and other rule violations.
All robots must pass the technical and safety checks before competing.
No preliminary online round or shortlisting; direct offline registration.
The top 3 teams play knockout matches to decide the final rankings.

competitions.name: Ideastrom
competitions.tagline: Pitch the idea. Defend the business.
competitions.incharge: Saurabh Ranjan, Club Secretary of E-Cell
competitions.about: IDEASTROM is the flagship E-Cell event of ProtoFos, an innovation and startup idea pitching competition. Teams submit an original startup or business idea and shortlisted teams pitch it live before a judging panel, moving from idea to execution to industry perspective.
rules: Round 1: Online idea submission, screened by the E-Cell panel for a shortlist.
Round 2: PPT-based live pitch, about 6-8 minutes of presentation + 3-4 minutes of Q&A (final timings fixed after the shortlist).
Every pitch must cover: problem statement; proposed solution; target users and market; innovation and differentiation; business model; feasibility; scalability; implementation roadmap.
competitions.judges: The invited guest speaker (subject to availability and consent), otherwise a panel of faculty, alumni entrepreneurs and invited professionals.
